notes: The session's web-search allowance ran out after seven searches, so nearly all of this part was found by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: campaign websites, government, party and newspaper sites, and those sites' own search pages where their robots.txt allows it. Which candidates had filed a campaign website was read from a scratch copy of the database on which the project's own filed-websites step had been run; the real database was only read. A filed address is listed here only where the site itself was opened and names the candidate and the office or place.

Sites that refused the reader or asked scripts to stay out, so nothing was taken from them and nothing was worked around: bradyhoag.com (a bot check, so Brady Hoag has no website finding and no own words here, although the Senate District 37 Republicans' page links to that address as his website); mohamudnoor.org (HTTP 402; the Senate District 60 DFL links to it, and the state DFL's list links his name to a social media page instead); mncourts.gov (403: no court page for Judge Engelking); mn.gov (a CAPTCHA page; not asked again); co.jackson.mn.us (robots.txt: no county page for Kristi Meyeraan); Red Lake County's site (its certificate does not match its name; the plain address is dead); albertleatribune.com, axios.com and Pine Knot News's search page (403); Ballotpedia (it answered a script with a blank page, and is not a source this sweep cites in any case); the search pages of star-herald.com, redwoodfallsgazette.com, wjon.com and maplegrovemn.gov, and the city sites of Rockville, Cold Spring and Richmond (robots.txt). The Jackson County Pilot and the Timberjay show only the opening lines of their stories to non-subscribers; only those lines were read.

Read and left out on purpose: ages printed in news stories, which do not fix a birth year; jobs, union posts, nonprofit boards and a party unit's chairmanship; an advisory task force and an association seat held as part of a council term (Kristy Barnett); a tribal police department's civilian advisory board (Dan Danielson); labor and personal endorsements; the Scott County Republicans' page 'Endorsed/Recommended Candidates', which links a banner image dated 2024 to Terry Stier's site with no text naming him, the office or the year. Not opened at all: the affidavits of candidacy the City of Moorhead posts (they carry home addresses), and news stories whose headlines were about a legal matter.

For the second reader: (1) Mark Johnson's campaign site carries a 2022 copyright line; it names him and the office and is the address Wikipedia gives as his official campaign website, but nothing on it is dated 2026. (2) Mark Johnson and Mohamud Noor are sitting members whose roster records have no birth date, so the Legislative Reference Library's is given, as part 0 did; the Library gives only the year for Noor. (3) Annie Harala: the Duluth News Tribune's August 5 story says both 'appointed to the seat in 2023' and 'since taking office in January 2023', while its August 12 story says she 'was elected to the St. Louis County Board in 2022'; only the start year 2023 is used. (4) Kristi Meyeraan's office has no end year because the one page found reports her appointment in April 2022 and nothing later; she is the only candidate for the office on the 2026 list. (5) Judge Engelking: the Morrison County Record's October 2020 list of 7th District Court judges 'all running unopposed' names 'Judge 8 - Matthew E. Engelking' (https://www.hometownsource.com/morrison_county_record/free/who-s-on-your-ballot-it-depends-upon-where-you-live/article_7cad71d6-1ad1-11eb-84c6-77ac39a70689.html), so the seat was his by 2020, but no page read gives the year he took the bench. (6) Michael Haatvedt's post is a seat on a city board that promotes tourism; whether a card shows it is John's decision. (7) Ryan Schatz's review item rests on a news report, not an official record: he stays on the ballot. (8) An 'Abdi Abdulle' lost the DFL primary for U.S. House District 2 on August 11; no page ties him to Abdirahman Ahmed Abdulle of the Rosemount council race (the questionnaire he answered speaks of earlier runs in Minneapolis and Lakeville), so nothing was recorded. (9) The Minneapolis DFL's 2026 endorsement for School Board District 5 went to the other candidate, so Molly Chase has own words but no endorsed_by.

Nothing was found beyond what they filed for Dennis Hartman, Al Kokesch, Chris Johnson (the Mesabi Tribune's story on his candidacy says he 'has never before run for elected office'), Kelly Brekke, Abdirahman Ahmed Abdulle, Alex Tierney, Richard (Rick) Rask, Kasey Wolters, Teresa Glass, Gary Distel and Joshua Hurt: no campaign website that could be confirmed, and no public office that a page states. Their cities', counties' and school districts' own pages of members, boards and commissions were read where they answer; none names them.

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's own downloader (30 pages, all answered). 41 findings were read against their pages: 39 kept, 2 removed, 2 reworded.
Mark Johnson's site names him and the office but carries a 2022 copyright line and no 2026 date; it is kept as the campaign's standing site, as the researcher noted.

The state DFL's endorsed page, the Clay County DFL's page and the Senate District 37 Republicans' page print no year in their text; the DFL page was last changed on 2026-09-16 and each lists this year's candidates.
Dassel-Cokato's page prints each member's terms after that member's own words; the line after Jenna Kantola's is 'Terms: 2023-2026'.
St. Louis County's page does carry the county's portraits of Annie Harala and Paul McDonald.
Nothing from the never-collected list is in any field. The pages themselves carry phone numbers, postal addresses and e-mail; none was copied.
